chapter: Radio color line, San Francisco and Columbia staff
title: Turning down Bob Crosby's radio show on Dave Klein's advice
summary: Offered three times the money on Bob Crosby's CBS show, Lee stayed on staff because Dave Klein said leaving would hurt the next black musician.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: You went back to Paramount? I mean Columbia?

Oh yes, I went back to Columbia, and then I had an offer right across the street again, at CBS, Bob Crosby had a 15 minute -- was it the Chesterfield Show, wasn't it? Do you remember that? Bob Crosby had a 15 minute ... it was on 5 days a week.

Now they came after me to do that. Okay. Now, here comes Father Klein again. I was gonna take it; there was no question about it. I mean I was definitely gonna take it. Now this time he did convince me that -- he was a

Jewish man, you know, and he told me -- he could tell me about this because the Jewish people had been through the same type of thing that the black people go through, but the things that you want to do -- the normal thing, it's -- it'll be construed that the people who follow you may not get a chance -- well, I was in the middle of the contract; you had to sign contracts, you know; when you were on staff, you signed a yearly contract. And so this was my 2nd year in about the 3rd month.
Now when they offered me this job, and this was like 3 times as much money a week, and 5 days a week ..
Which? You mean Bob Crosby was 3 times as much money as the studio?

Yes. Oh yes. And it was just 15 minute shows a day, and I'm sure -- I know it was the Chesterfield Show; as a matter of fact, Ralph Collier ended up getting the job. Ralph Collier was a drummer, a friend of mine; we used to practice together all the time.

But anyway, Dave Klein explained to me why I should not leave in the middle of my contract because it would make it bad for the next black person who wanted to get on staff, and so I shouldn't take it, and he convinced me.
So I didn't move. But they never did have anyone else on the staff, and I don't know whether it was because I did such a bad job or what, but I mean ..
Well, it couldn't have been that you were doing a bad job, or your contract wouldn't have been renewed.
